summary:
Prebuilt browser simulations for Isaac Lab documentation. Adds a compact 24-slab domino cascade, VBD cable bending, and Ant walking with steering and direct perturbations. Includes all earlier version directories unchanged.

Physics uses captured Newton Warp kernels compiled to CPU WebAssembly; Three.js renders the state and the shared JavaScript actor evaluates policy weights. The archive is served as static files and needs no simulation server.

[Preview gallery](https://maxkra15.github.io/isaaclab-browser-demos/v6/) · [Exporter reference #7974](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/pull/7974) · [Docs integration #8559](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/pull/8559)

Documentation deployment verifies the accompanying SHA-256 before staging the archive. Serve extracted files over HTTP for local previews.
title: isaac-sim/IsaacLab Interactive browser demos v6

summary:
MicroDuck warehouse interactions: convex colliders derived from enabled scene geometry, compound rack/pallet components, and 12 movable floor props. Other props and fixtures remain fixed. Free props use nominal 250 kg/m³ density and calculated mass/inertia.

Physics retains native BAM drives, the Newton constraint solver, 50 Hz policy control, and four 5 ms physics steps. Reset restores the captured robot and prop state. Robot/policy assets from v2 and warehouse visuals/textures from v4 are reused; v1–v4 remain unchanged in this archive.

[Play the preview](https://maxkra15.github.io/isaaclab-browser-demos/v5/?demo=microduck) · [Exporter source #7974](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/pull/7974) · [Docs integration #8559](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/pull/8559)

Source revision: `2c6eda6d0e8065b1b0af998c6774369453fcc7a7`.
Archive SHA-256: `08de8419b05815c629bc92d25826eee472cb6ee36d977f61611962ac977c4964`.

Validated native observations/graph replay, browser contact-driven prop motion, gravity, reset, room containment, mouse/touch controls, and public preview loading/stepping. The docs workflow stages this checksum-pinned archive; it does not compile WASM.
title: isaac-sim/IsaacLab Browser demos v5

summary:
Add edge-latched viewport joysticks and the bounded MicroDuck warehouse scene. Pull a stick back or press Escape to stop; arrows remain momentary. Turning from rest uses a visible 0.25 m/s forward assist. Robot dragging still applies 2 N.

The authored Factory meshes and base-color textures use 94 shared prototypes and 797 instances. The Newton/BAM simulation includes 25 static boxes for perimeter, shelf-row and clutter collisions. This is a browser adaptation of the scene, not the native training environment or complete warehouse dynamics. Original robot CAD and policy files reuse v2 assets.

Deploy the complete archive: v1, v2 and v3 are unchanged and v4 reuses their files. Attribution and warehouse asset license notices are included. Exporters: [#7974](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/pull/7974), source revision [0c89d1c46](https://github.com/maxkra15/IsaacLab/commit/0c89d1c460dbdf0bc066bd8be6e1d327bb1d9c18). Docs: [#8559](https://github.com/isaac-sim/IsaacLab/pull/8559).

Validation: native/captured walking and observation checks; all twelve demos; mouse/touch latching, cancellation, pause/reset, turning assist, mobile layout; four physical boundary contacts. Software-rendered browser playback measured about 95% of real time after visual mesh reduction.

SHA-256 (`isaaclab-browser-demos-v4.tar.gz`): `d0b21f7ba4d556181c3f32130a8bd1a456f16b3de2c2fff5cd8d810b9a159abf`.
title: isaac-sim/IsaacLab Browser demos v4

One way to find such utterances is to transcribe the speech and detect language alternation in the text, but this depends on obtaining accurate multilingual transcriptions.
